stem: Leininger's transcultural nursing theory proposes that culture provides which of the following?
options: The broadest and most important means that nurses can use to promote health and well-being
A narrow factor with no bearing on health promotion
A barrier that should be eliminated from nursing practice entirely
A concept relevant only to pediatric nursing

stem: According to Leininger, nursing is BEST described as which of the following?
options: Inherently a transcultural profession requiring transcultural care knowledge to give competent and necessary care to people from different cultures
A profession that should avoid any consideration of a client's cultural background
A profession limited strictly to biomedical intervention with no cultural component
A profession relevant only in multicultural nations

stem: According to Leininger, the ultimate goal of culturally-driven nursing is to assist, support, or enable individuals to do which of the following?
options: Maintain well-being, improve life, or face death
Avoid all contact with the health care system
Reject care from providers of a different culture
Rely solely on family members with no professional nursing involvement

stem: Leininger's theory is said to fit well with gerontology, geriatrics, and care of persons with disabilities because culture determines which of the following?
options: The societal values of an elderly person
The exact biochemical rate of cellular senescence
The genetic mutation rate of somatic cells
The precise hormonal decline curve in the neuroendocrine system

stem: According to Leininger's theory, the more value a culture ascribes to the elderly person, the more which of the following results?
options: Care and protection the society gives to the elderly
Isolation and neglect the society directs toward the elderly
Financial burden placed exclusively on the family with no societal role
Disengagement expected of the elderly from all social roles

stem: According to Leininger's theory, the concept of health and care that an elderly person receives is BEST described as which of the following?
options: Determined exclusively by national health policy with no individual variation

stem: Orem's Self-Care Deficit Theory of Nursing describes three concepts that are basic to nursing practice. Which of the following lists all three?
options: Self-care, self-care deficit, and nursing system
Self-care deficit, classical conditioning, and operant conditioning

stem: In Orem's theory, the 'nursing system' concept refers MOST to which of the following?
options: The basic activities that aid health promotion, well-being, and health maintenance
A behavior modification technique used to shape learner responses
A sociological theory describing societal roles of the elderly

stem: According to Orem's theory, the nursing system is viewed as which of the following?
options: Multidimensional and viewed as wholly compensatory, partially compensatory, or supportive-educative
A single fixed category with no variation across patients
Exclusively wholly compensatory for every patient regardless of ability
Exclusively supportive-educative for every patient regardless of ability

stem: Under Orem's theory, the role of the nurse is to provide education and support that help the patient do which of the following?
options: Acquire the necessary abilities to perform self-care
Remain entirely dependent on the nurse indefinitely
Transfer all care responsibility to family members exclusively

stem: Which of the following systems of the body shows the most obvious reflection of age as a person ages, according to the notes?
Integumentary changes related to ageing are linked to which of the following causes?
options: Internal (genetic) and external causes such as exposure to sunlight and environmental chemicals
Exclusively internal genetic causes with no external contribution
Exclusively external causes with no genetic contribution
A single isolated cause with no multifactorial contribution

stem: With ageing, melanocytes within the epidermis undergo which of the following changes?
options: Remain completely unchanged regardless of age
Migrate entirely to the dermis with no epidermal presence

stem: The dermal-epidermal junction flattens with age owing to the retraction of which of the following structures?
Flattening of the dermal-epidermal junction with age causes the skin to appear which of the following?
options: Exclusively darker with no change in thickness

stem: The dermis contains blood vessels that provide nutrients to the epidermis and assist in which of the following functions?
With ageing, collagen in the dermis, which makes up the major portion of the dermis, undergoes which of the following changes?
options: Decreases, leading to decreased elasticity and strength
Increases dramatically, leading to increased elasticity and strength
Remains completely unaffected by the ageing process
Is entirely replaced by melanin with no structural change

stem: Nail growth slows down around which decade of life, accompanied by a decrease in lobular size and peripheral circulation?
options: The sixth decade only, with no change before then

stem: With ageing, the nail plate undergoes which of the following changes?
options: Turns yellow and thick, causing the nail to become soft, brittle, and prone to splitting
Turns pink and thin, becoming more flexible and resistant to splitting
Remains completely unchanged in color and texture
Becomes transparent with no change in thickness

stem: Greying of the hair with ageing is the result of a decline in which of the following?
The primary musculoskeletal change in ageing, caused by ageing, is which of the following?
options: A change in stature and posture
An increase in bone density with no change in posture
An increase in height with age
A complete absence of any skeletal change with age

stem: The decrease in height seen with ageing of about 1 to 4 cm is mainly due to compression of which of the following structures?
options: The long bones of the limbs

stem: With ageing, bone absorption within the vertebral bodies, wrist, and hip increases due to a decrease in which of the following?
options: Collagen levels in the nail plate

stem: With ageing, there is a decrease in lean body mass with an increase in which of the following?
With age, the heart shows an increase in lipofuscin deposits in which of the following?
With ageing, the number of pacemaker cells in the sinoatrial node does which of the following?
With age, there is an increase in calcium deposits on the walls of the aorta and large vessels, leading to which of the following?
options: No change in blood pressure whatsoever
A decrease exclusively in diastolic pressure with no systolic change

stem: With ageing, the baroreceptors, which regulate blood pressure, become which of the following?
options: Less sensitive in the older adults
More sensitive in the older adults
Completely non-functional with no blood pressure regulation at all

stem: Musculoskeletal changes affecting the respiratory system in ageing include shortening of the thorax with an increase in which of the following?
With ageing, ventilation of the bases of the lung is decreased while ventilation of which part of the lung is relatively increased?
The gastrointestinal system of older adults may be characterized by decreased secretion, absorption, and which of the following?
options: A complete absence of any functional change

stem: After what age does the liver begin to shrink and enzyme production decrease, according to the notes?
Renal blood flow progressively decreases from approximately 1200 mL/minute to approximately how much by age 80, according to the notes?
With ageing, glomerular filtration rate (GFR) does which of the following, according to the notes?
With ageing, creatinine clearance does which of the following, and should be monitored before administration of drugs that depend on renal function?
options: Becomes undetectable by routine laboratory testing

stem: With ageing, there is little decrease in hormone secretion with the exception of which two hormones specifically named in the notes?
Hyperthyroidism in the elderly commonly goes undiagnosed because symptoms are more atypical than in younger populations, presenting with weight loss and which of the following?
options: Apathy, congestive heart failure, and atrial fibrillation
Enhanced energy and weight gain with no cardiac involvement
Improved appetite with no change in weight
A complete absence of any cardiac symptom

stem: There is still much that is unknown about nervous system changes with age, but experts believe there is a progressive loss of neurons primarily due to which of the following?
options: No change whatsoever in brain weight
A complete absence of any neuronal loss with age

stem: With ageing, the cerebral cortex dendrites shrink, reducing the number of fibres that receive synapses from other cells, resulting in which of the following?
options: No change whatsoever in impulse transmission
A complete absence of any dendritic change

stem: With age, sleep pattern changes occur, with stages 3 and 4 (deep sleep) greatly decreased while which of the following increases?
options: Frequent awakening and total awake time
The duration of REM sleep exclusively with no change in awakenings

stem: Visual changes of ageing include presbyopia, which is caused by rigidity and loss of elasticity of which structure?
Senile cataracts, the most common cause of adult blindness, are due to changes in which structure?
Presbycusis, a hearing change in ageing, is a sensorineural loss of hearing particularly affecting which of the following?
options: Only sounds below the range of human speech
A complete absence of any frequency-specific hearing change

stem: In males, ageing is associated with a decrease in testosterone production and testes decrease in size, along with which of the following changes?
options: A diminished viscosity of seminal fluid and decreased sperm count
An increase in seminal fluid viscosity and increased sperm count
No change whatsoever in reproductive function
A complete cessation of testosterone production at age 50

stem: Among health problems of the elderly, cataract, glaucoma, deafness, and reduced vision are grouped under which category?
Among health problems of the elderly, arthritis, heart disease, hypertension, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) are grouped under which category?
Among health problems of the elderly, dementia, depression, rigidity of our-look, and suicide are grouped under which category?
Among health problems of the elderly, Alzheimer's disease, cerebrovascular accident, and organic brain syndrome are grouped under which category?
Among health problems of the elderly, constipation, diverticulosis, fecal impaction, gallbladder disease, haemorrhoids, and hiatal hernia are grouped under which category?
Among health problems of the elderly, angina, atherosclerosis, congestive heart failure, hypertension, and myocardial infarction are grouped under which category?
Among health problems of the elderly, breast cancer, cervical cancer, vaginitis, benign prostate hypertrophy, impotence, and prostate cancer are grouped under which category?
Among nursing interventions for hypertension in the elderly, the nurse should monitor blood pressure and which of the following?
options: Only urine output with no weight monitoring
Only serum albumin level with no weight monitoring
Only stool pattern with no weight monitoring

stem: A recommended intervention for hypertension management in the elderly includes promoting a good balance between which two activities?
options: Dietary fat intake and dietary protein intake

stem: Which of the following is a recommended nursing intervention for an elderly client with cognitive impairment?
options: Correct underlying causes of disease if possible and provide a protective environment that reinforces reality
Avoid providing any assessment of the client's condition
Isolate the client from all personal hygiene assistance
Withhold emotional support from the family entirely

stem: Which of the following is a recommended nursing action for cancer screening in older women, according to the notes?
options: Promote monthly breast self-examination and yearly Pap smears and mammograms
Discourage any form of breast self-examination
Recommend screening only once in a lifetime regardless of age
Avoid any discussion of nutritional practices related to cancer risk

stem: Which of the following statements BEST reflects a consideration related to communication when assessing an older client's health status?
options: Older people tend to under-report symptoms of illness or describe them vaguely, making it difficult for the nurse to obtain relevant information
Older clients always report symptoms with perfect clarity and no vagueness whatsoever
Communication barriers never affect the assessment of older clients
Sensory or neurologic deficits have no bearing on an older client's ability to communicate

stem: According to Rice (2003), home care nursing is BEST described as which of the following?
options: The delivery of quality nursing care to patients in their home environment, intermittent or part-time
A form of care delivered exclusively in a hospital setting
A form of care that excludes any family involvement
A form of care limited strictly to institutional long-term facilities

stem: In the home care of the elderly, of importance is the care given in which setting, along with the cooperation of community resources?
Which of the following reflects a recognized role of the family in the home care of the elderly regarding physical comfort?
options: Helping the elderly meet the needs of activities of daily living such as bath, oral care, and other body grooming
Refusing to assist with any activity of daily living
Excluding the elderly from decisions about physical comfort entirely
Providing physical comfort only when a formal nurse is present

stem: Which of the following reflects a recognized role of the family in making the home environment handicap-friendly for an elderly person with disability?
options: Environmental adjustment including provision of physical structures that enhance the comfort of the client
Refusing to make any structural adjustment to the home
Removing all assistive devices from the home environment
Relocating the elderly person permanently to an institution regardless of preference

stem: Which of the following reflects a recognized responsibility of family members regarding the elderly member who becomes sick at home?
options: The family members usually provide the initial care before calling the attention of the nurse and others involved in care
The family should never provide any initial care and should wait exclusively for professional intervention
The family should discourage the elderly person from any further medical attention
The family has no role whatsoever in recognizing illness in the elderly member

stem: Which of the following reflects a universal precaution guideline for infection control in the home care of the elderly?
options: Hands should be washed with soap and water before and after contact with the patient
Hand hygiene is unnecessary in the home setting
Gloves should never be worn regardless of possible infection transmission
Sharp objects may be disposed of in any uncovered container

stem: Which of the following reflects a universal precaution guideline for infection control specifically regarding sharp objects and needles in home care?
options: Sharp objects and needles should be placed in protective disposable containers that can be sealed with a lid
Sharp objects should be left uncovered on any surface after use
Needles should be reused across multiple patients to conserve supplies
Needles should be disposed of in regular unsealed household trash

stem: Which of the following reflects a recommended infection control practice for daily home cleaning in the care of the elderly?
options: Encourage daily cleaning of the room with soap and water, washed daily, and well ventilated with enough light
Avoid cleaning the room more than once per month
Keep the room poorly ventilated to conserve heat regardless of infection risk
Avoid washing the room with soap and water under any circumstance

stem: Which of the following reflects a recommended practice for maintaining health at a high level in the elderly, according to the notes?
options: Eating a balanced diet, getting adequate amounts of sleep, rest, sunshine, fresh air, and exercise
Avoiding all forms of physical activity regardless of ability
Restricting fluid intake severely with no medical indication
Eliminating rest periods entirely to maximize daily activity

stem: CASE SCENARIO: An 84-year-old client from a culture that reveres elders is brought in by extended family who insist on participating in all care decisions and request that traditional remedies be incorporated alongside prescribed treatment. Which nursing theory BEST supports the nurse's approach of integrating the family's cultural practices into the plan of care?
options: Orem's self-care deficit theory applied in isolation from culture

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A client recovering from a stroke is completely unable to perform any self-care activities and requires the nurse to perform all bathing, feeding, and positioning. According to Orem's theory, which nursing system is being applied?
options: A system that requires no nursing intervention at all

stem: CASE SCENARIO: An 80-year-old client is noted to have thin, pale, translucent skin with visible blood vessels, a two-inch loss of height compared to his young-adult measurement, and nail plates that are thick, yellow, and prone to splitting. Which body system's age-related changes are being described in combination here?
options: Integumentary and musculoskeletal changes of normal ageing
Isolated cardiovascular changes with no skin or bone involvement
Isolated endocrine changes with no skin or bone involvement
Isolated neurological changes with no skin or bone involvement

stem: CASE SCENARIO: An elderly client is prescribed a standard adult dose of a hepatically metabolized medication. The nurse notes the client's liver has begun to shrink with reduced enzyme production, and serum albumin is low. Which nursing concern is MOST appropriate regarding this prescription?
options: The drug may accumulate in the body because of reduced metabolism and fewer protein-binding sites, increasing the risk of toxicity
The drug will be metabolized faster than in a younger adult with no risk of accumulation
Serum albumin level has no bearing on drug distribution in the elderly
Liver changes in the elderly do not affect drug metabolism at all

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A home care nurse visiting an elderly client's house for wound care routinely washes her hands before and after contact, places used needles in a labeled sealed sharps container, and wears gloves when handling soiled dressings. Which overall principle do these combined actions reflect?
options: Universal precautions for infection control in home care of the elderly
Orem's wholly compensatory nursing system exclusively
The disengagement theory of sociological aging
